::: {#sol-error-rate-curve}

::: {#fig-error-rate-curve}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   A staircase line of error rate against cutoff, from 0 to 16.
#|   Between its steps the line is flat.
#|   It falls in steps from the low cutoffs to a low, bumpy stretch at middle cutoffs,
#|   where it touches its lowest level on several short separate pieces,
#|   then climbs in steps toward the high cutoffs.
is_01 = (labels == 0) | (labels == 1)
ink_01 = center_ink[is_01]
is_one = labels[is_01] == 1

cutoffs = np.arange(0, 16.005, 0.01)
error_rate = np.array([np.mean((ink_01 > c) != is_one) for c in cutoffs])

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3), layout="constrained")
ax.plot(cutoffs, error_rate)
ax.set_xlabel(r"cutoff $\theta$ on center ink")
ax.set_ylabel("error rate")
plt.show()
```

The [error rate](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/metrics.html#def-error-rate) of the 0-or-1 rule among the `r sum(py$is_01)` images of 0s and 1s,
against the cutoff.
